# How does your free unlimited trial work?

Getting Started Updated 21.10.2026

First of all, we offer a free unlimited trial to let you try out our APIs and evaluate the efficiency of our service. To get a free trial, you should simply create an account with DataForSEO.

Once you are logged into the DataForSEO Dashboard you’ll see your API credentials for making calls from your API testing platform or through your preferred no-code tools and AI agents. Alternatively, you can use our built-in API Playground which allows you to make actual API calls and obtain real JSON data through a graphic user interface.

Note that upon registration free $1 credit for API testing will be added to your account balance. You can use this balance to make API calls for an unlimited period of time. However, this amount will be sufficient to make a limited number of API requests.

$1 will be enough to get, for example:

  * 800+ SERPs with high-priority tasks
  * 14,000+ backlinks with Rank values and other data
  * 16,000 keywords with Google Ads metrics

Note that there is no need to create another trial account to make more test APIs calls. This will be considered a violation of DataForSEO Terms of Service, and such an account will be suspended.

If you feel that you need to test our service with larger API request volumes, we offer a free Sandbox feature for API testing and configuration. In case this option does not suit you and you still would like to test a higher request volume, contact us, and we will find a solution together.

# DataForSEO Dashboard: how to find everything and more

Account & Billing Updated 18.11.2026

The DataForSEO Dashboard is a graphic user interface for managing your account and controlling API usage. You can use it to check your account balance, find and manage API credentials, update account details, monitor spending, review task IDs and errors, make test API requests, manage billing, browse database samples, and access support.

This guide explains how to use the main dashboard features based on what you want to do.

Contents:

  * Start testing with your free trial balance
  * Find and use your API credentials
  * Check your account balance
  * Understand where your funds are going
  * Control spending and prevent unexpected costs
  * Add funds and manage payments
  * Troubleshoot failed API requests
  * Browse and purchase large datasets
  * Use documentation to understand requests and responses

The API Playground is a built-in API explorer that lets you make API calls through a simple graphic interface and view results instantly in JSON format. Please note that the API Playground sends real API requests, so using it may consume your account balance. Learn more about this option for API testing from our dedicated article.


#### Find and use your API credentials

To make requests to DataForSEO API, you need your API credentials. You can find them in API Access section.

Connect DataForSEO to Any Tool: API Key Guide

Once you log in to your DataForSEO Dashboard, you can open this section from the left-hand navigation menu or by using the shortcut in the top bar. Clicking either option will open the API Access section where your API credentials are.

The API credentials include:

  * API login — a unique, automatically generated string used to identify your account when making API requests.
  * API password — a secure password automatically generated by DataForSEO for API authentication.

You can use these credentials to connect DataForSEO APIs to tools like Postman, Make, n8n, Google Sheets connectors, or your own applications.

Changing your API login

If you need to update your API login, you can do so in the API Access section of your Dashboard.

Keep in mind that your API login is used to authenticate API requests. After changing it, make sure to update the credentials in any applications, integrations, or workflows connected to DataForSEO.

API password visibility and recovery

Your API login always remains visible in the Dashboard. Your API password is visible only during the first 24 hours after registration. After that, it is hidden for security reasons. If you need your API password later, click Send by e-mail, and the password will be sent to the email address you used to create your DataForSEO account.

Base64-encoded API credentials

For the first 24 hours after registration, the API Access tab displays a ready-made, Base64-encoded string of your `login:password`.

### DataForSEO API key: FAQ

#### How do I get my DataForSEO API key?

Create a free account, log in, and open the API Access tab in the dashboard sidebar. Our system generates your API login and API password, and the two, encoded in Base64, are your API key. On older accounts, the login may still be your sign-up email. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

#### Where do I find my API password?

It’s in the API Access tab of your dashboard. Don’t confuse it with your account password: that one logs you into the dashboard, and only the API password works for API requests. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

#### Why can’t I see my API password in the dashboard?

The dashboard shows your API password for the first 24 hours after registration, then hides it for security reasons. After that, click Send by e-mail and we’ll resend it to the address on your account. Jump to Step 1: get your API credentials

#### Is the DataForSEO API key the same as my login password?

No. Your login password only gets you into the dashboard. The API key is built from a separate API password that our system generates for you, and mixing the two up is one of the usual reasons a request fails. Jump to Common authentication mistakes

#### How do I encode my DataForSEO credentials with Base64?

Join your login and API password with a colon (`login:password`) and encode that string with Base64. You can copy a ready-made encoded string from the API Access tab in the first 24 hours and request it by email after that, or make one yourself with a trusted online encoder or a one-line terminal command. Make and n8n do the encoding for you, so you can skip this step there. Jump to Step 2: encode your credentials with Base64

### Step 1 — Get your API credentials from the dashboard

Create a free account on our website. New accounts get a $1 trial credit, and the SERP Google Organic Live Advanced endpoint costs $0.002 per call, so the trial covers around 500 live Google SERPs before you spend a cent. Enough room to set things up and run a few tests.

Once you’re logged in, open the API Access tab in the dashboard sidebar. Two things most teams trip on here:

  * Your API password is not the same as your account password. The account password gets you into the dashboard. The API password authenticates your API requests, and our system generates it automatically when you sign up. You don’t pick it.
  * Your API password is visible for the first 24 hours after registration, then hidden for security reasons. If you missed the window, click Send by e-mail, and we’ll resend it to the address on your account. For a full walkthrough, see our help article on finding everything in the DataForSEO Dashboard.

Now you have your API login and API password. On an older account, the login may still be the email you signed up with. The next step is to combine them into a format that an HTTP request can carry.

# DataForSEO API Playground: a handy way to test APIs

Getting Started Updated 18.11.2026

API Playground is a built-in solution that allows testing DataForSEO APIs without API testing tools (e.g., Postman, Soap UI, Apigee, and so on). It makes actual API calls and provides real JSON data through a graphic user interface.
API Playground is available within the DataForSEO dashboard. To access it, log in to your account or create one if you haven’t already.

Once signed in, you can make requests to the following APIs:

  *     * SERP API;
    * Keyword Data API;
    * OnPage API;
    * Business Data API;
    * DataForSEO Labs API;
    * Backlinks API.

 

Note: since the tool makes actual API calls, you will be charged for each request made. The price depends on the used API and the specified parameters.
